title: The Weathered Ridge Descending Nowhere

features.name: the eroded waymarker
features.desc-on-touch: once this tower showed direction. the weather has worn it into ambiguity. now it points everywhere and nowhere at once.

features.name: the ridge that forgets its own slope
features.desc-on-touch: you stand on a ridge so weathered that the concept of climbing or descending has become philosophical. the ground cannot remember whether it is rising or falling.

features.name: the weathering glyph
features.desc-on-touch: what was written on this plaque has been worn to nothing. the absence itself is now what you read—the archive learns to store empty text.

features.name: the wind-carved pool
features.desc-on-touch: water has gathered here but the wind refuses to let it stay. it evaporates before it can remember being still. motion rendered as absence.

inscription: the ridge has learned that being weathered is indistinguishable from being pathless; everything here descends into its own disappearance

file.note: log of passages becomes increasingly fragmentary; later entries describe slope and weather becoming the same phenomenon

a slope that might be descent or wind—both leading to the same nowhere
toward the lower places where weather has forgotten what weather meant
